correctness.rationale: Writing Q_i=sum_j x_ij², S=sum_i Q_i, the graph product gives x²=0 iff S-Q_i=0 for all i; summing gives (r-1)S=0. When char p does not divide r-1 this is the independent system Q_i=0; at resonance each Q_i equals unrestricted t. Classical odd-q diagonal Gauss sums give the stated parity-sensitive fiber counts T_n(t), whose products produce the exact piecewise census. For p∤(r-1), quadratic cones of dimension n_i-1 have binary splitting only when n_i=2, yielding 2^b geometric components, Frobenius pairing when χ(-1)=-1, and rational span determined by isotropic vectors. For p|(r-1), equations Q_i-Q_r form a complete intersection of dimension N-r+1; flatness of torsion-free k[t]-modules, generic smoothness over t≠0 and Cohen–Macaulay equidimensionality prove geometric reducedness. Differencing points with one ±1 coordinate supplies a basis of the rational span; K_{p+1} yields 2^p rational lines. Independent small-field direct counting matched eight actual quadratic-equation systems, including q=3 and q=5 K_(2,2), and the resonance p=3 r=4. Counts are not substituted for arbitrary q or scheme-theoretic proof.
